newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan finance minister rules out rupee change.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan finance minister rules out rupee change.

text.p: Pakistani Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz on Friday ruled out any early downward adjustment of the rupee against international currencies.
"I do not see any need for an exchange rate adjustment at the moment," he told Reuters Financial Television just ahead of his budget speech for fiscal 1997/98 (July-June).
He said the previous government led by Benazir Bhutto had devalued the rupee by 30 percent against the dollar during its three-year term, but this had failed to stimulate exports.

Aziz said that any new devaluation would raise the cost of debt servicing, already equivalent to 70 percent of total tax revenue, and increase the cost of imported raw materials, which might discourage industrial revival.

"Devaluation also leads to higher cost of imported goods and therefore to inflation," he said. "If we succeed in stabilising our inflation and our budget deficit, then we can maintain a more stable exchange rate in line with the world currencies."
